subject: AuroraAI — midterm upsize & conversion path for Dedicated pool
messages:
From: Megan Lewis <megan@auroraai.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-27T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Mid-term capacity increase / converting burst to reserve — AuroraAI

Hi Logan,

Quick question — our product team is seeing a consistent uptick in inference volume for the search-ranking feature (roughly +52% RPS last 30 days). We have three months left on our current Dedicated commit (12x A100-equivalent GPUs) and would like to explore options to add capacity mid-term.

Concretely, we're evaluating: 1) converting some of our existing burst credits into a reserved commit (bought down monthly) and 2) adding +4 GPUs to the pool now vs waiting to the renewal. Procurement wants order-of-magnitude pricing, lead times for hardware allocation, and whether there are SLAs or throughput guarantees that change if we move to a larger pool mid-contract.

Can you share a one-page sketch of the options and a preliminary quote? I can loop in procurement (procurement@auroraai.com) or calendar a quick call.

Attached: procurement questionnaire (short form).

Thanks —
Megan
VP Product | AuroraAI
megan@auroraai.com

Attachment: Procurement_Questions_Aurora.pdf (PDF, 92 KB)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-28T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Mid-term capacity increase / converting burst to reserve — AuroraAI

Hi Megan — thanks for the note and the context. We can certainly support both conversion of burst to reserved commit and an immediate +4 GPU top-up. Two quick asks so we can size and price accurately:

- Can you share a 7/30/90-day token/RPS profile (p95 latency target) or a few sample traces?
- Are you currently using 16bit or 8bit quantized models in prod? That affects per-GPU throughput assumptions.

High-level options I'll brief below and Laura will follow up with commercial. Monica is cc'd for throughput estimates and lead time.

Options (rough sketch):
- Option A: Convert 50% of burst credits into a 6-month reserved commit (soft discount tier) — fastest to enable, no infra reprovision.
- Option B: Immediate +4 GPUs to pool (keeps commit unchanged) — results in higher instantaneous throughput; may require node rebalancing (estimated 2-week lead time).
- Option C: Convert burst -> reserved + immediate +2 GPUs now, +2 GPUs at renewal (phased ramp) — balances cost and commitment.

I can send a short quote tomorrow. Would you prefer a call Friday 10–11 PT?

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.com

Megan / Logan — technical note from infra:

Summary: adding +4 GPUs (A100 equivalent) to your pool should increase sustained throughput by roughly 33% under current model mix (assuming current 16-bit kernels). If you switch to 8-bit/quantized kernels we estimate a further 1.6–1.9x token throughput per GPU for generative workloads, but latency p95 will vary by sequence length.

Assumptions and risks:
- Baseline: measured on your last 30-day traces (sparse prefix reuse) — avg sequence length 128 tokens; batch sizes ~8.
- Rebalancing: node-level KV cache warm-up is ~45–90 minutes for full traffic switchover; during warm-up we may see elevated tail latency for rarely used prefixes.
- Compatibility: if you run custom kernels we need a quick CI verification; otherwise this is standard.

Lead time: 10–14 business days for capacity allocation + testing (we can accelerate to ~7 business days with a small expedite fee in the quote).

Attached: Throughput_Estimates_Aurora.csv (per-GPU QPS/throughput across common model families).

If you want, we can schedule a short engineering deep-dive to validate numbers against a replay trace.

—Monica
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

Attachment: Throughput_Estimates_Aurora.csv (CSV, 28 KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-01-30T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Proposed commercial options — AuroraAI midterm upsize

Megan — following Logan and Monica's notes, here's a commercial sketch. Attached is a formal quote (Aurora_Dedicated_Quote_v2.pdf) with line items. Highlights below: 

1) Phased conversion (recommended) — convert 50% of unused burst credits into a 6-month reserved commit and add +2 GPUs immediately. Pricing: incremental monthly commit priced at 10% below current month-on-month rate if you commit for the remainder of term (3 months) and then convert to a 12-month renewal at standard reserved pricing.

2) Immediate upsize (+4 GPUs) — list price for +4 GPUs with standard reserved-rate discount at your current tier. We can offer a one-time onboarding credit (equivalent to 5% of the incremental monthly cost) to offset rebalancing/testing overhead. SLA: same uptime SLA applies; throughput guarantees (p95 latency target) are provided after a short qualification period (2 weeks) and with the new pool size pinned.

3) Flexible step-up — a step schedule that allows +2 GPUs now and +2 GPUs at renewal with a stepped discount curve (higher discount at renewal). This preserves flexibility and avoids a long-term uplift if you want to validate.

Discounting and approvals: based on your ARR and commitment band we're able to offer up to 18% standard discount on incremental commits; deeper discounts require approval from sales ops (Aditya is cc'd).

Next steps: I attached the quote and a short SOW addendum describing how the pool will be rebalanced and the acceptance criteria for throughput. If you want tightened SLA language we can include it in the addendum (subject to legal review).

Attachment: Aurora_Dedicated_Quote_v2.pdf (PDF, 210 KB); SOW_Addendum_Aurora.docx (DOCX, 45 KB)

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Account Lead | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

- Is there a minimum commitment term if we convert burst credits to reserved?
- What is the exact SLA / credit language for throughput regressions during the 2-week qualification window?
- Can we have a hard cap on the expedite fee?

Procurement attached a short list of questions (attached). Happy to take a call — Kyle (cc'd) will own the procurement redlines.

Megan
